C’est l’action de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force toute-puissante, \v 20 qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a déployée dans le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité d’entre les morts et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a fait asseoir à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite dans les lieux célestes, \v 21 bien au-dessus de toute principauté et de toute autorité, de toute puissance et de toute souveraineté, et de tout nom qui puisse être nommé, non seulement dans cet âge-ci, mais aussi dans l’âge à venir.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que, depuis que j’ai entendu parler de votre foi dans le Seigneur Jésus et de votre amour pour tout le peuple de Dieu, \v 16 je n’ai pas cessé de remercier Dieu pour vous. Je pense toujours à vous quand je prie. \v 17 Je demande au Dieu de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, le Père glorieux, de vous donner {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit, qui vous rend sages et vous montre comment est Dieu, pour que vous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaissiez vraiment. \v 18 Je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demande d’ouvrir les yeux de votre cœur et de les remplir de lumière, pour que vous compreniez trois choses. Vous saurez quelle espérance {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a donnée quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a appelés. Vous saurez combien {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint est glorieux et précieux pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : c’est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} héritage, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trésor. \v 19 Et vous saurez combien {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance est grande pour nous qui croyons. Rien ne peut se comparer à elle. C’est la même force puissante \v 20 que Dieu a utilisée quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a ressuscité le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} d’entre les morts. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donné la place d’honneur, à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite, dans le ciel. \v 21 Là, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est bien au-dessus de tous les chefs et de toutes les autorités, de toutes les puissances et de tous les seigneurs, et de tout nom que l’on peut invoquer. Il est au-dessus d’eux, non seulement dans le temps présent, mais aussi dans le temps à venir.

decisions.choice: because of this: because of all God has done for them in Christ (verses 3-14)
alternatives: because of their faith and love only
decisions.reason: Διὰ τοῦτο looks back to the blessings just praised, and especially to the readers' share in them (verses 13-14). Hearing of their faith and love, Paul gives thanks and prays.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "and the love toward all the holy ones"
alternatives: "your faith in the Lord Jesus and toward all the holy ones", without "love"
decisions.reason: Several of the earliest manuscripts, among them P46 and Codex Vaticanus, do not have τὴν ἀγάπην, which leaves faith directed both to Jesus and to the holy ones. The words may have dropped out when a copyist's eye skipped between the two forms of the article. Faith and love together are Paul's usual pair (Colossians 1:4). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of wisdom and revelation: the Holy Spirit, who gives wisdom and reveals God
alternatives: a spirit of wisdom: a wise and perceptive frame of mind
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα has no article and could mean a disposition ("a spirit of wisdom"). But only God's Spirit gives revelation, and Isaiah 11:2 promises the Messiah "the Spirit of wisdom". The readers have already received the Spirit (1:13), so Paul is praying that the Spirit will do this work in them, not that they receive him for the first time. On either reading the wisdom comes from God.

decisions.choice: the Father of glory: the glorious Father, to whom glory belongs
decisions.reason: Like "the glory of his grace" (verse 6), the phrase describes: the Father is glorious (compare "the God of glory", Acts 7:2; Psalm 29:3).

decisions.choice: in the knowledge of him: so that they come to know God more fully
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to God, the subject of the sentence. ἐπιγνώσει is knowledge that is personal and full, not information only (as in Colossians 1:9-10).

decisions.choice: the eyes of the heart enlightened: inner understanding opened, so that one sees what God has done
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the center of thought and will, not only of feeling. Light for the eyes of the heart is understanding given by God (Psalm 19:9; 2 Corinthians 4:6). The participle describes the state Paul prays for, as part of the gift of verse 17.

decisions.choice: three things to know: the hope of his call, the riches of his inheritance, the greatness of his power
decisions.reason: The three questions each begin with τίς or τί ("what"). The first looks back to God's call, the second to what he will gain in his people, the third to his power now at work.

decisions.choice: the hope of his calling: the hope God gave them when he called them
decisions.reason: God's call brings a sure hope with it (4:4, "one hope of your calling"): the inheritance and the final redemption of verse 14.

decisions.choice: his inheritance in the holy ones: God's own inheritance, which is his people
alternatives: the inheritance God gives, which his people share
decisions.reason: κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ is "his", God's, inheritance. In the Old Testament Israel is the Lord's inheritance (Deuteronomy 9:29; 32:9), and verses 11 and 14 have spoken of God's people as his portion and his possession. The other reading takes it as the inheritance God gives, to be shared among his holy people (Colossians 1:12). Both are taught in Scripture; the question is which Paul means here.

decisions.choice: his power beyond all measure: Paul heaps up four words for strength to stress how great it is
decisions.reason: ὑπερβάλλον means "surpassing". Paul adds δυνάμεως, ἐνέργειαν, κράτους and ἰσχύος: power, working, might, strength. The words overlap; together they say that no power is greater than the one at work for believers.

decisions.choice: seated at his right hand: the place of honor and rule, as promised in Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (Psalm 110:1) is applied to Christ's exaltation again and again in the New Testament (Mark 12:36; Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13). Verse 22 goes on with a related psalm.

decisions.choice: rule, authority, power, lordship: ranks of unseen spiritual powers, and every other power that has a name
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of the time named ranks of angels and spirits with words like these. In Ephesians the rulers and authorities are in the heavenly places (3:10) and include powers hostile to God's people (6:12); Colossians 1:16 and 2:10 use the same terms. "Every name that is named" takes in any power anyone could name or call on, as people did in prayers and spells (Acts 19:13-19 shows such practice in Ephesus).

decisions.choice: this age and the age to come: the present time and the new age God will bring
decisions.reason: Jewish teaching divided history into the present age and the age to come (Matthew 12:32). Christ's rule over every power holds now and will hold in the age to come.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}" in verse 20; {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of wisdom and revelation
alternatives: a spirit of wisdom and revelation
decisions.reason: All three levels follow m3. Literal brackets "the", since the Greek has no article.

decisions.choice: thanking God for you
decisions.reason: Thanks are given to God; Balanced and Readable say so, as Colossians 1:3 does.

decisions.choice: how rich and glorious an inheritance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people (B); how glorious and precious {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people are to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: they are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own treasured inheritance (R)
alternatives: the riches of his glorious inheritance among the saints
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m9.

decisions.choice: every ruler and authority, every power and dominion (B); every ruler and authority, every power and lord (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Colossians 1:16. "Ruler and authority" is kept at every level, as in the Ephesians word list, so that 3:10 and 6:12 can be traced back here.

decisions.choice: in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer phrase from the Ephesians word list.

decisions.choice: so that you will understand three things; Nothing can compare with it; God gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the place of honor at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand
alternatives: so that you may know what is the hope...; surpassing greatness; seated him at his right hand
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences, says plainly that there are three things to know (m7), and explains "surpassing" and "right hand" (m10, m11).

decisions.choice: every name anyone can call on
decisions.reason: Readable says what naming a power meant (m12).

decisions.choice: gobierno y autoridad y poder y señorío (L); gobernante y autoridad, poder y dominio (B); gobernante y autoridad, poder y señor (R)
decisions.reason: "Principado" now usually means a small state ruled by a prince, and "potestad" is old-fashioned. The words follow the English, so that the same powers can be traced in 3:10 and 6:12.

decisions.choice: resucitándolo ... sentándolo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek participles as Spanish gerunds, and a pronoun joined to the end of a verb cannot take a capital. Balanced and Readable use the separate pronoun "lo", which carries the setting.

decisions.choice: enzi hii ... enzi ijayo
decisions.reason: αἰῶνι is an age, a period of history (m13). "Ulimwengu" would blur it with "the world" of verse 4 ("ulimwengu"); "enzi" (era) names a time.

decisions.choice: utawala, mamlaka, uweza, ubwana (L); mtawala, mamlaka, uweza, ubwana (B); mtawala, mamlaka, uweza, bwana (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as the English list, kept at every level so that the powers of 3:10 and 6:12 can be traced back here. For the whole letter.

decisions.choice: principauté, autorité, puissance, seigneurie (L); principauté, autorité, puissance, souveraineté (B); chefs, autorités, puissances, seigneurs (R) (for the whole letter, 3:10, 6:12)
decisions.reason: The same French words as in Colossians 1:16 and 2:10, 2:15, so that the unseen powers (m12) can be traced through both letters. "Principauté" is the established French name for this rank of powers; Readable says "chefs" because "principauté" is now mostly a small country.

decisions.choice: l’action du pouvoir de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force (L); l’action de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force toute-puissante (B)
decisions.reason: Paul heaps up words for strength (m10), and "puissance" is already used for the word in the line before; Literal keeps three distinct French words so the heaping can still be seen.

source.text: καὶ πάντα ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν κεφαλὴν ὑπὲρ πάντα τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἥτις ἐστὶν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν πληρουμένου.

records.literal_gloss: And all things he subjected under the feet of him, and him he gave [as] head over all things to the church, \v 23 which is the body of him, the fullness of the [one] the all things in all filling.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} subjected all things under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] head over all things to the church, \v 23 which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, the fullness of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who fills all things in all.
en.B: God has put all things under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the church to be head over all things. \v 23 The church is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body. It is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness, filled by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who fills everything in every place and every way.
en.R: God has put everything under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over all things. God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} head over all things, and has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a gift to the church. \v 23 The church is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, and it is full of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He fills all things completely.

es.L: Y sometió todas las cosas bajo {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dio [como] cabeza sobre todas las cosas a la iglesia, \v 23 la cual es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo, la plenitud de aquel que llena todas las cosas en todo.
es.B: Dios ha puesto todas las cosas bajo los pies {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha dado a la iglesia como cabeza sobre todas las cosas. \v 23 La iglesia es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo. Es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} plenitud, llenada por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, que lo llena todo en todo lugar y de todas las maneras.
es.R: Dios ha puesto todo bajo los pies {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} reine sobre todas las cosas. Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha hecho cabeza sobre todas las cosas, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha dado como regalo a la iglesia. \v 23 La iglesia es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo, y está llena de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Él llena por completo todas las cosas.

sw.L: Na vitu vyote alivitiisha chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na alimtoa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [awe] kichwa juu ya vitu vyote kwa kanisa, \v 23 ambalo ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utimilifu wa yule anayejaza vitu vyote katika vyote.
sw.B: Mungu ameweka vitu vyote chini ya miguu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na amemtoa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa kanisa awe kichwa juu ya vitu vyote. \v 23 Kanisa ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Ni utimilifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, uliojazwa na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayejaza kila kitu kila mahali na kwa kila namna.
sw.R: Mungu ameweka kila kitu chini ya miguu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ili atawale juu ya vitu vyote. Mungu amemfanya kuwa kichwa juu ya vitu vyote, na amemtoa kama zawadi kwa kanisa. \v 23 Kanisa ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, naye amelijaza. Yeye hujaza vitu vyote kabisa.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a soumis toutes choses sous {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a donné [pour] tête au-dessus de toutes choses à l’Église, \v 23 qui est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps, la plénitude de celui qui remplit tout en tous.
fr.B: Dieu a tout mis sous les pieds du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a donné à l’Église pour être la tête au-dessus de tout. \v 23 L’Église est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps. Elle est {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} plénitude, remplie par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, qui remplit tout, en tout lieu et de toute manière.
fr.R: Dieu a tout mis sous les pieds du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} règne sur toutes choses. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a fait chef de toutes choses, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a donné à l’Église comme un cadeau. \v 23 L’Église est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps, et elle est remplie de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il remplit tout complètement.

decisions.choice: he put all things under his feet: Psalm 8:7, applied to Christ
decisions.reason: Psalm 8:7 says of humankind, "you have put all things under his feet". Paul changes "you" to "he" and applies the line to Christ, the man in whom God's purpose for humankind is fulfilled, as 1 Corinthians 15:27 and Hebrews 2:6-9 also do. With Psalm 110:1 in verse 20, it pictures Christ ruling over every power.

decisions.choice: God gave Christ, head over all things, to the church
alternatives: God made Christ head over all things for the sake of the church
God made Christ head of the church
decisions.reason: τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ is the one Christ is given to: the head over all things is God's gift to the church, and rules for its good. That he is also head of the church follows in verse 23 (and 4:15; 5:23), but here "over all things" is the point.

decisions.choice: head: the one who rules over all, and the body's source of life
decisions.reason: κεφαλὴν here means authority "over all things"; with "his body" in verse 23 it also brings in the picture of the head that holds the body together and gives it growth (4:15-16; Colossians 1:18; 2:19).

decisions.choice: church: God's people as a whole, everywhere
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ is the gathered people. In Ephesians it always means the whole church, Christ's one body (3:10, 21; 5:23-32).

decisions.choice: the church is Christ's fullness: filled by him and with him
alternatives: the church completes Christ, who would be incomplete without it
"the fullness" describes Christ, not the church
decisions.reason: πλήρωμα stands next to "his body" and most naturally describes the church. In Ephesians the church is what Christ fills: Paul prays they will be filled to all the fullness of God (3:19), and Christ gives gifts to bring the church to "the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ" (4:13). Colossians 2:9-10 says the same: in Christ dwells all the fullness, and in him believers have been filled. That Christ needs the church to complete him is possible grammatically but fits the rest of the letter poorly.

decisions.choice: who fills all things in every way: Christ is the one who fills
alternatives: who is being filled in every way (by God, or by the church)
decisions.reason: πληρουμένου can be passive ("being filled") or middle with an active sense ("filling"). The object τὰ πάντα shows that he fills something, and 4:10 says Christ ascended "so that he might fill all things". ἐν πᾶσιν means "in every way" or "in all places".

decisions.choice: God has put all things under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
alternatives: he subjected all things under his feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who subjects, and Christ, under whose feet all things are put, since the pronouns alone would be unclear.

decisions.choice: so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over all things; has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a gift to the church
alternatives: gave him as head over all things to the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what the psalm picture means and makes plain that Christ is given to the church (m2).

decisions.choice: it is full of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He fills all things completely
alternatives: the fullness of him who fills all in all
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m5 and m6 in plain words, using "full" and "fill" as the Ephesians word list allows.

decisions.choice: utimilifu
decisions.reason: "Ukamilifu" is completeness or perfection; "utimilifu" is fullness, being filled up, and is the word used for "the fullness of the times" in verse 10, so the two uses of πλήρωμα stay one word. Readable says it with the verb "kujaza" (fill).

decisions.choice: la tête (L, B), chef (R); l’Église, with a capital, for the whole church (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Tête" keeps the picture of head and body that the next verse and 4:15-16 and 5:23 build on (m3); Readable says "chef" for the ruling sense. As in Colossians, the capital in "l’Église" marks God’s people as a whole (m4), not one congregation or a building.
